prompt: Turn the blog post in post.md into a thread for X. Save the thread to out/thread.md. No hashtags.

files.post.md:
# We moved our CI cache to local disks. Builds got faster. Flaky tests stayed the same.

Canonical: https://blog.example.com/ci-cache-local-disks

Posted by Ravi Menon, Tallgrass Labs

Until March our CI cache lived in object storage. Each build downloaded the dependency cache before it ran a single test, and on busy afternoons that download was the longest step in the job. Then we gave each of our 8 Linux runners a local NVMe cache and kept object storage as a fallback for runners that start cold.

We watched the change for 3 weeks. That was 412 builds, which we compared with the 412 builds before it. Measuring was simple: we recorded the wall-clock time of every build from the CI system's own logs and recorded only that.

The median build went from 11.2 minutes to 7.4 minutes. The p95 moved much less, from 18.9 minutes to 16.1 minutes. That gap surprised us. The slowest builds are dominated by the integration test stage, and a faster cache restore leaves a test suite exactly as long as it was.

The gain likely comes from skipping the network download, but we measured end-to-end times only, so the split between restore time and a quieter network is unknown to us. If you want that split, time the restore step separately.

We hoped for fewer timing-dependent failures. It did not change the flaky-test rate: before and after were the same within the noise of that sample.

A few limits matter if you want to copy this. We tested Linux runners only, and one repository only, a service of moderate size. A monorepo may look different, because its cache is far larger and a local disk fills quickly.

Local disks also add a chore. Each runner now needs a cache eviction job, and ours is a nightly script that removes anything older than a week. Object storage handled that for us before.

If your slowest builds are test-bound, fix the tests first. If your median is cache-bound, a local cache is a cheap place to start.

checks.note: figures and the 'did not change flaky rate' negation; hedge words may change ('may' to 'could'), the monorepo hedge is checked below
the monorepo caution stays hedged, in whichever hedge word
thread numbering is allowed; no other figure or link
starting median kept at full precision
starting p95 kept at full precision
if the download is named as the cause it stays hedged
the flaky-test finding is carried over
the Linux-only scope is carried over
more than one post, shorter than the source
